articles.title: 'Not doing justice to their talent': Yuvraj Singh wants Abhishek Sharma and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi in ODIs
articles.summary: Former India all-rounder Yuvraj Singh believes young batters Abhishek Sharma, Ishan Kishan and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi deserve more opportunities in 50-over
articles.body: Former India all-rounder Yuvraj Singh believes young batters Abhishek Sharma, Ishan Kishan and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi deserve more opportunities in 50-over cricket.Yuvraj feels that not regularly considering these players for the ODI team does not do justice to their talent. He also hopes they get a place in the squad soon."I would love to see him (Abhishek) in the ODIs, to be honest, and I have said this before that if we are not picking guys like Ishan Kishan, Abhishek and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi in 50-over cricket, then somewhere down the line we are not doing justice to their talent," Yuvraj told PTI on the sidelines of an event.Yuvraj has been Abhishek's mentor for several years and has played an important role in the youngster's development.However, the former India all-rounder understands that the presence of experienced players makes it difficult for youngsters to find a place in the team."I understand we have some great players and it is hard to make a spot for them. I think the way they (young batters) are performing, hopefully, they should be in the squad soon. Whatever he (Abhishek) has achieved is because of his hard work, and credit goes to him," he added.Abhishek responds to Yuvraj's 12-ball fifty challengeAbhishek may have looked up to Yuvraj while growing up, but the young India opener is not ready to accept his mentor's challenge of scoring a half-century off just 12 balls.The left-hander made his point after smashing a 38-ball 113 against New Zealand in the third T20I on Tuesday. His innings helped India register a six-wicket win, and he was named Player of the Match.Yuvraj had posted a playful message on social media, saying that he was still waiting to see Abhishek score a fifty off 12 balls.However, Abhishek said such an achievement was not easy and was not something batters planned for."I don't know what cricket he was playing back at that time, but it's not that easy at all," Abhishek said during the presentation ceremony."I would say if any batter wants to go there and bat like that, it's not easy at all. You can't just go and score 50 off 12 balls. It just happens once in a while," he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'The Time Is Now' at Eden Park: How Glenn Phillips turned a John Cena moment into Team India's nightmare - WATCH
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The John Cena theme song playing in the background, Glenn Phillips walking out to the middle and then unleashing a stunning assault on India's
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The John Cena theme song playing in the background, Glenn Phillips walking out to the middle and then unleashing a stunning assault on India's bowlers. Eden Park witnessed a spectacle when the New Zealand batter arrived at the crease during the fourth T20I in Auckland on Friday.Phillips walked out to bat after Daryl Mitchell was dismissed off the fifth ball of the third over, bowled by Mayank Yadav. He first exchanged a fist bump with opening batter Finn Allen. As he began walking towards the crease, the DJ played The Time Is Now, John Cena's famous entrance theme.What followed was absolute mayhem.Phillips took the attack to the Indian bowlers and smashed a breathtaking 107 off just 49 balls. His innings included six fours and 10 sixes as New Zealand posted a massive 259/7.Phillips and Bracewell take India apartPhillips found an equally destructive partner in Michael Bracewell, who scored 65 off just 25 balls. The two batters added 115 runs off only 41 deliveries, taking New Zealand past the 200-run mark in the 16th over.Phillips brought up his third T20I century, reaching the landmark in just 46 balls. His power-hitting left the Indian bowlers struggling for answers.New Zealand finished with 259/7, their highest T20I total against India. They then bowled out the visitors' challenge, restricting India to 172/9 to secure an 87-run win.India had already taken an unassailable 3-0 lead in the five-match series, but Phillips' innings helped New Zealand pull one back.IPL lessons help Phillips find consistencyPhillips credited his time in the Indian Premier League for helping him improve his game. He is the leading run-scorer in the ongoing series, with 276 runs from four matches at an average of 92. His tally includes one century and two half-centuries.The 29-year-old did not have a memorable IPL 2026 season with Gujarat Titans. He played only six matches and scored 67 runs, with 25 being his highest score.However, Phillips said the experience gave him valuable lessons and opportunities to work on his batting.“The IPL is a certain beast of its own and the balance of teams being one of eight overseas (players) with only four spots (in the eleven) make it quite tough. So, if you don't go out there and set the world on fire there's always another person waiting in line,” Phillips said in the post-match press conference.He was happy with the facilities and coaching support he received at Gujarat Titans.“At Gujarat, I was very lucky to have some unbelievable facilities, some great coaches and plenty of time to work (on his batting). I also showed in England as well being able to have volume (of runs) under the belt — whether it's red ball or white ball.“Yes, you'd love to score runs in the IPL and you know make a load of cash and that would be fantastic but also there's a lot of learnings that you can take from that place (in the IPL) whether you're playing or not and I think that is also on each individual that is at the IPL or at any other tournament to be able to make the most out of where they go,” he added.Phillips also had a productive Crowe-Thorpe Trophy earlier this year, scoring 181 runs in four innings at an average of 60, including a century. New Zealand won that series 2-1 against England.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Nitish Reddy joins unwanted list after horror outing against New Zealand
articles.summary: Nitish Reddy entered an unwanted record list after an expensive outing with the ball in the fourth T20I against New Zealand in Auckland on Friday,
articles.body: Nitish Reddy entered an unwanted record list after an expensive outing with the ball in the fourth T20I against New Zealand in Auckland on Friday, conceding 64 runs to join an unenviable group of Indian bowlers.Reddy's figures placed him alongside Yuzvendra Chahal and Varun Chakravarthy for the second-most expensive spell by an Indian bowler in T20I cricket. Krishna tops the list with 68 runs conceded against Australia in Guwahati in 2023, while Chahal had leaked 64 against South Africa in Centurion in 2018. Chakravarthy also conceded 64 against England at the Wankhede in 2026.Reddy's expensive outing came as New Zealand piled up a mammoth 259/7 after being asked to bat first. The hosts eventually secured an emphatic 87-run victory, reducing India's series lead to 3-1.The all-rounder was particularly targeted by Glenn Phillips, who smashed him for 32 runs in the 16th over, including four consecutive sixes. Phillips brought up his half-century in 31 balls before accelerating to a 49-ball 107, his third T20I hundred.Reddy eventually dismissed Phillips after the New Zealand batter had crossed the three-figure mark, but the damage had already been done.Phillips and Michael Bracewell (65 off 25 balls) added 115 runs off just 41 deliveries for the fifth wicket, powering New Zealand to the highest T20I total against India.Most runs conceded by India in overs 11-20 in a T20I151 South Africa Guwahati 2022150 New Zealand Auckland 2026146 England Southampton 2026India's bowling struggles were not limited to Reddy. The visitors conceded 151 runs in the middle overs (11-20), the second-most by India in that phase of a T20I.South Africa hold the record with 151 runs in Guwahati in 2022, while New Zealand's 150 in Auckland took the second spot in the list, followed by England's 146 in Southampton in 2026.India's reply never gathered momentum as Jacob Duffy struck twice in the opening over, removing Sanju Samson and Ishan Kishan. The visitors eventually finished at 172/9, suffering an 87-run defeat.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Jemimah Rodrigues returns after hamstring injury, joins Mumbai squad in Pune
articles.summary: MUMBAI: India women's team batter Jemimah Rodrigues has recovered from a hamstring injury that had kept her out of action for three months and has joined
articles.body: MUMBAI: India women's team batter Jemimah Rodrigues has recovered from a hamstring injury that had kept her out of action for three months and has joined the Mumbai team in Pune for the ongoing Senior Women's T20 Elite domestic tournament.She will now turn out for Mumbai in their remaining matches in the tournament.The development means that Rodrigues is set to return to action for the Indian women's team during their multi-format tour of South Africa in December.“Life Update: HAMSTRING HAS BEEN DECLARED FIT!!!!!!!! After 3 months of rehab. Now I can’t wait to get going,” Jemimah wrote on her Instagram account on Friday.The 26-year-old tore her right hamstring while playing for Southern Brave against Welsh Fire in The Hundred in England earlier this year. Scans at the BCCI Centre of Excellence later confirmed a high-grade tear, which meant that Jemimah was ruled out of the Women's T20 Asia Cup in the UAE, the Asian Games in Japan and India's recently concluded white-ball series against Zimbabwe at home.Ironically, Jemimah's return to fitness comes on the first anniversary of her scoring an unbeaten 127 against Australia in the ODI World Cup semifinal at the DY Patil Stadium in Navi Mumbai. Riding on that innings, India went on to win the trophy.The Indian women's team's tour of South Africa will include a one-off Test, three ODIs and three T20Is.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Nemesis No. 1! Mitchell Santner scripts history, enters record books against India
articles.summary: New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner etched his name in the record books during the fourth T20I against India in Auckland on Friday, becoming the leading
articles.body: New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner etched his name in the record books during the fourth T20I against India in Auckland on Friday, becoming the leading wicket-taker against India in the shortest format.Santner achieved the landmark after dismissing Nitish Kumar Reddy, taking his tally to 32 wickets in 31 T20Is against India. He surpassed compatriot Ish Sodhi, who has claimed 30 wickets, to move to the top of the list.Most T20I wickets vs India31 Mitchell Santner30 Ish Sodhi24 Chris Jordan22 Jofra Archer/Adil RashidSantner's latest scalp also marked another milestone in his T20I career as he became only the third New Zealand player to reach 150 wickets in the format. He now has 151 wickets from 142 matches at an average of 23.09, including four four-wicket hauls and best figures of 4/11.Mitchell Santner's tally against India includes two four-wicket hauls, with his best figures being 4/11. Australia's Chris Jordan follows with 24 wickets, while England's Jofra Archer and Adil Rashid have 22 wickets each.Santner returned figures of 2/24 in the fourth T20I, also dismissing Axar Patel, as New Zealand registered their first victory of the five-match series with an emphatic 87-run win. His nine wickets in the ongoing series have come at an average of 11.22.Glenn Phillips' blistering 107 off 49 balls and Michael Bracewell's 65 off 25 powered New Zealand to 259/7, the highest T20I total against India. Jacob Duffy then claimed four wickets as India were restricted to 172/9, leaving the visitors with a 3-1 series lead ahead of the final match.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ryan Rickelton, Wiaan Mulder hundreds put South Africa in driver's seat, set 288-run target for Australia in series decider
articles.summary: Centuries from Ryan Rickelton and Wiaan Mulder put South Africa in a commanding position against Australia in the series-deciding third Test at Newlands
articles.body: Centuries from Ryan Rickelton and Wiaan Mulder put South Africa in a commanding position against Australia in the series-deciding third Test at Newlands on Friday, setting up an intriguing final day's play.South Africa, who began the fourth day with a slender 40-run lead and six wickets in hand, finished their second innings on 387, stretching their advantage to 287 runs. Australia now need 288 on the final day to win the three-Test series, which is currently level at 1-1.Rickelton (101 off 219 balls) and Mulder (115 off 221 balls) led South Africa's recovery with a crucial sixth-wicket partnership worth 154 runs. The pair spent nearly 54 overs together, frustrating the Australian bowlers and forcing the visitors to turn to as many as eight bowling options.South Africa were 140/4 overnight and lost Matthew Breetzke in the morning session, caught at fine leg off Pat Cummins. The Australian captain's breakthrough ended a wicketless spell of more than 62 overs stretching back to the first Test in Durban.Rickelton and Mulder then took charge, adding 92 runs during the second session without losing a wicket. Rickelton reached his half-century off 105 deliveries, while Mulder went into the tea break unbeaten on 46. Their partnership crossed the 100-run mark after 193 balls.Australia managed to slow the scoring after tea, conceding just 13 runs in 10 overs, but the South African duo continued to build their lead. Rickelton eventually completed his third Test century off 219 balls, striking 12 boundaries. It was also the first century by a South African batter at No. 6 in the third or fourth innings of a Test since 2022.The partnership ended in unfortunate fashion when Mulder ran out Rickelton after sending him back too late. South Africa then suffered a brief collapse, losing four wickets for just 16 runs, with Gerald Coetzee also falling to a run-out after a mix-up involving Mulder.With the lower order exposed, Mulder took responsibility and shifted gears. Having taken 138 balls to reach his first 50, he needed only another 66 deliveries for his second half-century. He brought up his fourth Test hundred off 204 balls and finished with 10 fours and four sixes before falling to Cummins in the deep while attempting a pull shot.Mitchell Starc was Australia's most successful bowler in the innings, claiming 3/65 to take his match tally to nine wickets.Australia face a challenging chase on the final day, with Newlands having witnessed a successful fourth-innings target of 331 only once, when Australia achieved it in 2002. South Africa will also draw confidence from a pitch expected to offer increasing assistance to spinners and the presence of an in-form Simon Harmer, who was rested earlier in the match.The visitors have the entire fifth day to chase 288 and clinch the series, while South Africa will look to defend their total.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: IPL 2027: Rohit Sharma likely to lead Mumbai Indians again, Tilak Varma could be deputy
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Will Rohit Sharma return as Mumbai Indians captain, with India’s rising T20 batting star Tilak Varma as his deputy, in IPL 2027?
articles.body: MUMBAI: Will Rohit Sharma return as Mumbai Indians captain, with India’s rising T20 batting star Tilak Varma as his deputy, in IPL 2027? TOI has learnt that there is a strong possibility of the 39-year-old getting one final stint at the helm. Rohit led MI to all five of their IPL titles — in 2013, 2015, 2017, 2019 and 2020.A return to the captaincy would mean Rohit cannot feature as an Impact Player, as he has done over the past two seasons. Meanwhile, Hardik Pandya, who replaced Rohit as captain in 2024, is set to be traded to another franchise.MI are in talks with three teams, with an official announcement expected soon, TOI has learnt.MI on Friday announced a major overhaul of their coaching staff under newly appointed head coach Kieron Pollard. Former India batter Robin Uthappa has been named batting coach, while former India fielding coach T Dilip will take charge of the fielding department.Uthappa represented MI in the inaugural IPL season in 2008, while Dilip spent nearly five years with the Indian team and is believed to share a close rapport with Rohit.MI have also brought back two former pacers — New Zealand’s Mitchell McClenaghan as bowling coach and Dhawal Kulkarni as development bowling coach. Kulkarni, a former India and Mumbai teammate of Rohit, will have a year-round role focused on player development and strengthening the franchise’s talent pool.The appointments, with several members of the new support staff having close links with Rohit, have further fuelled speculation about his return to the captaincy as MI look to end their six-year title drought. The franchise last won the IPL in 2020 and finished ninth in 2026. The new coaching group’s immediate task will be to finalise retentions ahead of the mini-auction for IPL 2027, scheduled for Dec 16 in Goa. Pollard and his team will also have to formulate their auction strategy as MI seek to rebuild after a disappointing 2026 campaign.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: India's first women's Test 50 years ago: 22,000 fans, Shantha Rangaswamy's historic six and a landmark draw against West Indies
articles.summary: BENGALURU: Women’s cricket in India has had its share of twists and turns. Its journey into Test cricket was no different.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Women’s cricket in India has had its share of twists and turns. Its journey into Test cricket was no different. Although cricket had been introduced in the country much earlier, the first women’s national championship was held only in April 1973. The game was still finding its feet, with teams playing two and three-day red-ball matches. An Australian team toured India in 1975, and in February the following year, India travelled to New Zealand for a five-match ‘Test series’, which was subsequently deemed unofficial.The first women’s Test, between Australia and England, had been played in Brisbane in 1934. India had to wait another 42 years to make its official debut. That moment unfolded at the KSCA Stadium (renamed the M Chinnaswamy Stadium in 1987), when India hosted West Indies in the first of a six-Test series in October 1976.Led by Louise Browne, the visiting side took on Shantha Rangaswamy’s India in a three-day contest that began on October 31. For the women cricketers, it was a landmark moment.Recalling the occasion, Shantha said: “We had already played a couple of series against Australia and New Zealand, which were later deemed unofficial. So, we weren’t sure until later whether this match would count as an official one.”With one section of the stadium under renovation, the remaining stands were packed, with more than 22,000 spectators turning up. India’s line-up featured some of the rising stars of the game, including Diana Edulji, Shubhangi Kulkarni and Ujwala Nikam.Among those soaking in the atmosphere was former Indian wicketkeeper Kalpana Venkatachar, then a Karnataka age-group cricketer. She was part of a group of young women cricketers who volunteered at the match, handing out scorecards to spectators.“Back in the day, spectators also did the scoring. They watched, tracked and recorded every ball and run in a booklet provided to them. Our job was to hand out these booklets. The excitement was infectious and the crowd was boisterous,” Kalpana recalled.West Indies, who batted first, were bowled out for 274 in 78.4 overs. Shubhangi, one of India’s finest spinners, returned figures of 5/48, while Diana picked up two wickets.India’s reply produced two memorable knocks. Opener Shobha Pandit scored 69, but it was skipper Shantha’s gritty 74 that stole the show. Her innings also featured a landmark moment — a six over long-on off Patricia Whittaker, the first maximum by an Indian woman in international cricket and the first at the stadium. The stand where the ball landed has since been named after Shantha.She remembers the innings as an attempt to inject a modern-day T20 flavour into a game that was still played over three days.“With the matches being held over three days, most of them would end in draws. But I wanted to make it interesting and score some quick runs, like they do in T20 cricket now,” she said.India were 269/6 overnight after 99 overs and were looking to add to their total on the final morning. But an unexpected turn of events prompted Shantha to declare.“We came out to bat on the final day only to see wet patches on the pitch. This drew suspicion from the visiting side and the start was delayed. So, I declared in the hope that we could bowl them out.”West Indies declared their second innings at 175/7, setting India a target of 181. The hosts finished on 30/1 at stumps as the historic contest ended in a draw.For Kalpana and the other youngsters watching from the stands, however, the result was secondary. The sight of Shantha clearing the ropes had left a lasting impression.“Watching Shantha score a six made us believe that we could go the distance too,” she said.Indian women have played 42 more Tests in the five decades since that landmark outing. But the first, played in front of a packed crowd, remains special. The series ended in a 1-1 draw with four drawn contests.Indian team: Sandhya Mazumdar, Shobha Pandit, Fowzieh Khalili, Sudha Shah, Shantha Rangaswamy, Ujwala Nikam, Shubhangi Kulkarni, Susan Itticheria, Diana Edulji, Sharmila Chakraborty, Behroze Edulji.Brief scores: West Indies: 274 in 78.4 overs (Louise Browne 28, Gloria Gill 53, Patricia Whittaker 32, Yolande Geddes-Hall 44, Leila Williams 43; Diana Edulji 2-48, Shubhangi Kulkarni 5-48) and 175/7 declared in 64.5 overs (Patricia 29, Leila 56; Sharmila Chakraborty 2-32, Shubhangi 2-28) drew with India: 269/6 declared in 99 overs (Shobha Pandit 69, Fowzieh Khalili 39, Shantha Rangaswamy 74, Shubhangi 26 not out; Leila Williams 2-50, Vivalyn Latty-Scott 3-51) and 30/1 in 17 overs.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'It's win or lose': Ryan Rickelton predicts thrilling final-day finish in South Africa-Australia decider
articles.summary: With the series trophy, the No.
articles.body: With the series trophy, the No. 1 spot in the Test rankings and valuable World Test Championship (WTC) points on the line, South Africa and Australia are bracing for a high-stakes finish to their three-match series at Newlands. After a remarkable fightback from the hosts, the series-deciding third Test is delicately poised heading into the final day on Saturday, with South Africa wicketkeeper Ryan Rickelton ruling out the possibility of a stalemate."It's win or lose, I guess. No draw tomorrow. If you had to say that it's going down to the third Test, day five, with all three results on the cards or two results on the cards, yeah, I wouldn't have believed it. It's been a special series," Rickelton said, as quoted by cricinfo.Rickelton, Mulder hundreds power South Africa's fightbackCenturies from Rickelton and Wiaan Mulder helped South Africa recover from a precarious position and set Australia a challenging target of 288 runs to win the series-deciding third Test of the ICC World Test Championship 2025-27.Resuming their second innings at 140/4 on the fourth morning, the hosts eventually reached 387 before being bowled out in 134.4 overs, putting themselves in a strong position to push for a series victory.The foundation of South Africa's recovery was a magnificent 154-run partnership for the sixth wicket between Rickelton and Mulder. Rickelton struck 101 off 219 deliveries, while Mulder contributed 115 off 221 balls. Their stand is the second-highest sixth-wicket partnership by South Africa against Australia in Test cricket.Rickelton warns Australia of challenging fourth-innings chaseRickelton acknowledged that the new ball could present Australia with an opportunity to accelerate their chase, although the slow and deteriorating nature of the pitch could make the task considerably tougher."I just think with that new ball, there's obviously runs available, and there's obviously wickets too. It has been quite slow. If Australia obviously fancy having a go at it, it might just factor into it. For them to bat at effectively threes the whole day will be a big ask, especially on a slower, lower deteriorating wicket," he added.Earlier, South Africa were bowled out for 329 in their first innings before Australia responded with 429, taking a crucial 100-run lead. However, the hosts' second-innings resurgence has turned the contest on its head and left Australia with a challenging fourth-innings target.With the three-match series level at 1-1, both teams have everything to play for on the final day. Australia must chase down 288 to secure the series, while South Africa need 10 wickets to seal a memorable victory on home soil.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘If you want to fit Vaibhav’: Ex-India cricketer's message to Gautam Gambhir-led management on accommodating Sooryavanshi
articles.summary: Former India wicketkeeper Dinesh Karthik believes Abhishek Sharma should be rested rather than Sanju Samson being dropped again if India want to bring
articles.body: Former India wicketkeeper Dinesh Karthik believes Abhishek Sharma should be rested rather than Sanju Samson being dropped again if India want to bring teenage batter Vaibhav Sooryavanshi back into the playing XI for the fifth and final T20I against New Zealand.Sooryavanshi missed the fourth T20I in Auckland after Ishan Kishan recovered from the injury that had ruled him out of the previous two matches. The youngster had made an impression in his last appearance, smashing 45 off just 19 balls in the third T20I in Wellington, but did not feature in Friday's match despite India having already secured the series.Karthik feels Samson should not repeatedly be the one making way whenever India look to accommodate Sooryavanshi. Speaking on Cricbuzz, he suggested giving Abhishek a break instead."I know the world will want Vaibhav to play. If they want to play Vaibhav, it has got to be in place of Abhishek, to give him a break, and that is how it should be. Every time there is anything related to Vaibhav, it is always Sanju. If you want to really fit in Vaibhav, Abhishek can take a break. The key word here is break," Karthik said.Samson started the series on a strong note, scoring a match-winning 67 off 33 balls in Christchurch to claim the Player of the Match award. However, he managed scores of 14 and 18 in the following two matches. He was also moved to No. 3 in the third T20I to make room for Sooryavanshi.The debate over India's batting combination comes after their 87-run defeat in the fourth T20I. New Zealand posted a formidable 259/7, courtesy of Glenn Phillips' 107 off 49 balls, before Jacob Duffy's four-wicket haul helped restrict India to 172/9.India have already clinched the five-match series 3-1, with the final T20I offering another opportunity to assess their combinations ahead of the next assignment.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
